chunks: And my father and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on them both) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'The heavens wept over al-Husayn ibn 'Ali and Yahya ibn Zakariyya, and they did not weep over anyone other than them.' I asked: 'And what is their weeping?' He said: 'They remained for forty days; the sun rose with redness and set with redness.' I asked: 'Is that their weeping?' He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: How did the heavens weep for Imam al-Husayn and Yahya ibn Zakariyya?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the heavens wept over the martyrdom of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali and Yahya ibn Zakariyya, manifested by the sun rising and setting with a red hue for forty days, a sign unique to these two figures. This narration, found in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, highlights the cosmic significance of their deaths in Shia tradition, linking the celestial mourning to the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophets. The forty-day period mirrors the duration of mourning rituals, emphasizing the enduring impact of their sacrifice on the spiritual landscape of the universe.
